name: Call Senior
description:
I aim to build the voice OS for f&b in India. 

Project Description (Refined + Structured)

This project is the convergence layer above DeepCall, incorporating elements of GrowwMaxx, to build a category-defining product: the Voice OS for restaurants — internally referred to as “Senior.”

Core Vision

Build the default AI voice infrastructure for the HORECA industry, starting with restaurants in India.
Senior is not just a tool — it is a full-stack system that owns, optimizes, and replaces voice interactions across the customer journey.

Product Stack

1. Evaluation & Training Layer (DeepCall)

AI-powered simulated calls to train and evaluate frontline staff
Solves for high attrition and inconsistent service quality in F&B
Immediate wedge into the market (low friction, clear ROI)

2. Voice Agent Layer (Senior)

AI voice agents handling reservations, queries, upselling, and customer interactions
Comparable to global players (e.g., Certus-style systems) but localized for India’s HORECA workflows
Becomes the primary revenue and retention engine

3. Voice Model Evaluation Layer (DeepCall / Future Product)

Evaluates performance of AI voice agents (not just humans)
Long-term: expands beyond F&B into a cross-industry voice QA layer
Strategic Insight

Voice agents will inevitably replace large parts of human-led call handling.
This creates a platform risk for DeepCall as a standalone product.

However, this same shift creates a distribution advantage:

DeepCall becomes the entry point (training + evaluation)
Senior (voice agents) becomes the upgrade / retention layer
DeepCall evolves into infrastructure for both human and AI evaluation

Instead of being disrupted by voice models, this stack allows us to own the transition.

Why This Works
F&B has extreme staff churn, making continuous training essential
Voice interactions are high-frequency, high-impact touchpoints
No dominant, India-first voice infrastructure player exists for this segment
Existing global solutions are not optimized for local accents, workflows, or cost sensitivity

Business Model Direction

Phase 1 (Now):
Launch DeepCall → acquire restaurants through training + evaluation use case

Phase 2:
Upsell Senior voice agents → automate customer interactions

Phase 3:
Expand DeepCall into AI agent evaluation infrastructure

Phase 4 (Optional Expansion):
Extend beyond F&B into hospitality, retail, and other voice-heavy industries
End State

A vertically integrated Voice OS for hospitality, where:

Every customer call during peak times is handled by AI

Every interaction (human or AI) is continuously evaluated

Restaurants rely on a single system for training, automation, and optimization

SENIOR

Voice AI Concierge for Indian Restaurants
Product Requirements Document · v2.0 · May 2026 · Zoronal Architecture
Design Partner
The Blue Door Cafe (TBDC), Khan Market, Delhi
v0 Build Window
5 days (owner + manager internal test)
Pilot Target
1 restaurant → 5 paying by Day 60
Unit Economics
₹4/call · 76–88% gross margin
Confidential — Not for Distribution

Contents

1. Product Overview 2. Problem Statement 3. Goals & Non-Goals 4. Target Users 5. MVP Scope 6. User Journeys 7. Functional Requirements 8. Non-Functional Requirements 9. System Architecture 10. Tech Stack 11. Metrics & Success Criteria 12. GTM & Business Model 13. Risks & Mitigations 14. Future Roadmap 15. Build Plan

1. Product Overview

Senior is an inbound voice AI concierge for restaurants in India. Maya, Senior's AI agent, picks up 100% of inbound calls, captures reservations, answers FAQs, and routes complex requests to the manager — all in under 2.5 seconds on Indian PSTN. Built on Zoronal's voice infrastructure with a Supabase data layer and Telegram ops loop, Senior deploys for a new restaurant in 5 days with zero telephony engineering.

Senior is built on three architectural principles: Zoronal handles the voice plane; Supabase owns all data (portable, vendor-neutral); everything between them is a single Edge Function. Swapping voice vendors is a 2-week project, not a rebuild.

The Direct Booking Flywheel

Maya actively offers callers a 15% weekday dinner discount for booking via this line instead of District or EazyDiner. The customer saves money. The restaurant saves the 10–20% aggregator commission. Senior pays for itself from the first direct booking it captures.

One-Line Pitch

Never miss another reservation call — Senior picks up every call, captures every booking, and costs less per month than 4 hours of front-desk staff time.

2. Problem Statement

A Delhi cafe misses 30–60 inbound calls a month during peak hours. Staff are serving tables. The phone rings out. The customer books on Zomato or District — paying a 10–20% aggregator commission that cuts directly into the restaurant's margin. For a 250–300 call/month restaurant with a 20% miss rate, that is 50–60 missed booking conversations — roughly ₹25,000–35,000 in recoverable reservation revenue walking out the door every month.

ROI Scenario Model

All scenarios use 45% reservation intent, 80% conversion, 80% show-up, ₹2,000 weighted AOV, 15% direct booking discount as additional retention lever.

ScenarioCalls/DayCalls/MonthMiss RateRes. IntentRevenue RecoveredSenior CostROI
Base515010%7₹8,960₹4,9991.8×
Mid824020%22₹28,160₹4,9995.6×
High1545020%41₹52,480₹4,99910.5×
Validation Required

250–300 calls/month and 20% miss rate are founder-surveyed assumptions (n=15). Validate against Blue Door's actual call logs in Week 1. Mid scenario (5.6×) is the working assumption for the GTM deck.

Why Existing Solutions Fail

SolutionHow Used TodayWhy It Fails
Human staffPicks up between service dutiesMisses 20%+ at peak; inconsistent info
District / EazyDinerAggregator listing10–20% commission; restaurant loses direct relationship
WhatsAppSome share a numberAsync; manager response lag 15–60 min
Generic IVRPress 1 for reservationsZero intelligence; customers drop immediately
US/UK voice AIN/A in IndiaNot built for Hinglish, Indian PSTN, or sub-₹10k pricing

3. Goals & Non-Goals

v0 Goals — Days 1–5 (TBDC Internal Test)

  1. Owner and manager validate the end-to-end flow: call → Maya captures → Telegram notification → Confirm/Decline → visible in Supabase Studio.
  2. Prove Maya handles Blue Door's knowledge card accurately (<2% false info rate) on 20+ internal test calls.
  3. Validate capacity check, weekend walk-in rule, and escalation flows function correctly.

v1 Goals — Days 6–15 (Blue Door Production)

  1. Prove Senior captures ≥80% of inbound reservation calls with correct data at Blue Door.
  2. Validate manager ops loop with WhatsApp + SMS (once accounts approved).
  3. Achieve <2.5s p50 end-to-end latency on real PSTN (confirmed working — maintain).
  4. Demonstrate 100% pickup rate on Senior Plivo DID.
  5. Generate case study artifact to close restaurants #2–5 by Day 60.

Non-Goals — Explicitly Excluded from v0 and v1

FeatureReason ExcludedTarget
Customer SMS (v0)No MSG91 creds yetv1
WhatsApp notifications (v0)No Meta Business account yetv1
Custom dashboardSupabase Studio + Zoronal suffice for first 5 restaurantsv1.5
Voice ordering3-month build minimum. One wrong order kills the pilot.v3
Real-time table availability6-week build; capacity cap covers 80% of the problemv2
Outbound remindersInbound only for MVPv1.5
POS / EazyDiner integrationChain ICP requirement; Stage 1 ICP doesn't need itv1.5
Caller memory / loyaltyRequires CRM + DPDP consent frameworkv1.5
Staff training moduleMonth 2 retention leverv1.5
Live PSTN call transferIndian PSTN transfer unreliable; message+callback is safe fallbackEvaluate v1.5
Multi-restaurant onboardingBlue Door only for v0/v1; generalise at customer #2v1.5

4. Target Users

Stage 1 ICP — MVP (Customers 1–10, Days 1–60)

DimensionDefinition
FormatIndependent owner-operated cafe or casual-dining restaurant
Size1–3 outlets; 30–80 covers per outlet
GeographyDelhi-NCR only (Khan Market, South Delhi, GK, Defence Colony, Hauz Khas)
Call volume≥5 inbound calls/day (150+/month)
Buyer personaFounder-owner. Single decision-maker. Buys on ROI and trust. 1–2 conversation close.
Design partnerThe Blue Door Cafe (TBDC), 66 Khan Market, Delhi

Stage 2 ICP — Scale (Customers 10–50, Days 60–180)

DimensionDefinition
FormatMulti-outlet Delhi chain: Cafe Delhi Heights, Social, Smoke House Deli tier
Size5–20 outlets; 60–150 covers per outlet
Gating conditionDo NOT approach chains until EazyDiner integration is live (v1.5). They will reject Google Sheets backend.

End Users — Callers

User TypeBehaviourWhat Maya Must Do
Reservation callerCalls to book. High intent. Time-pressured.Answer in <1.5s. Capture in <90 seconds. Mention 15% weekday discount.
FAQ callerHours, dietary, location, delivery, alcohol.Answer from knowledge card only. Offer to book if relevant.
Weekend walk-inCalls Sat/Sun before 1 PM wanting to book.Explain walk-in only before 1 PM, quote 15–20 min wait. Do not attempt to book.
Complaint callerUnhappy with food, service, previous booking.Never handle. Collect number, promise manager callback in 1 hour. Escalate immediately.
Older / less digital callerSlower speech, prefers voice, may speak Hindi.0.9× TTS speed, patient, switch to Hindi naturally.

5. MVP Scope

v0 — Included (Days 1–5, Internal Test Only)

Reservation slot-fillName (spell-back), phone (last 4 confirmed), party size, date, time, special requests.P0

15% direct booking discountMaya mentions discount for weekday dinner (7–11 PM) when reservation detected.P0
Capacity checkcheck_capacity tool fires to Supabase Edge Function before confirming slot.P0

Escalation flowComplaints, groups >15, modifications → collect number, promise callback, Telegram to manager.P0
Post-call webhook → SupabaseZoronal POSTs call data at hangup. Edge Function writes reservation to DB.P0
Telegram notification to managerInline buttons: Confirm / Decline / I'll Call Back. Manager taps to update status.P0
Owner view — Supabase StudioOwner views all reservations, call records in Supabase Studio. Zero custom build.P0

v1 — Added (Days 6–15, Production at Blue Door)

FeatureDescriptionPriority
WhatsApp to managerReplaces/supplements Telegram once Meta Business Account approved.P0
SMS to customerConfirmation SMS on manager confirm; decline + alternative on manager decline. MSG91.P0
Auto-confirm SLA30 min same-day / 4 hr future — auto-confirms if manager doesn't respond.P1
Knowledge card update flowManager texts change → LLM extracts → confirm → Supabase update → Zoronal prompt update via API.P1

Overflow forwardingAfter 30 days clean operation: main Blue Door number unanswered after 3 rings → Maya.P1

6. User Journeys

Journey 1 — Weekday Reservation (Happy Path + Discount)

[Customer calls at 6:45 PM on a Tuesday. Plivo DID → Zoronal → Maya picks up.]

MAYA:     Hi, this call may be recorded. This is Maya from The Blue Door Cafe —
          are you calling to make a reservation, ask a question, or speak to the manager?

CUSTOMER: Reservation. Tonight, dinner.

MAYA:     Lovely. What time were you thinking?

CUSTOMER: 8 PM, for 4 people.

MAYA:     Perfect. Quick note — if you book on this line for weekday dinner, you get
          a 15% discount. That's only when booking directly here, not on District
          or Zomato. Want to go ahead?

CUSTOMER: Yes, absolutely.

MAYA:     Great. Can I have your name?

CUSTOMER: Rohan.

MAYA:     Just to confirm — R-O-H-A-N, Rohan?

CUSTOMER: Yes.

MAYA:     And the best number to reach you?

CUSTOMER: 98xxx 3421.

MAYA:     Perfect — ending in 3-4-2-1. Any special requests for tonight?

CUSTOMER: Quiet corner if possible.

MAYA:     Noted. So that's a table for 4 tonight at 8 PM, under Rohan, ending in 3421,
          quiet corner preferred, with the 15% weekday discount applied.
          Sound right?

CUSTOMER: Yes.

MAYA:     Done. Your request is with the manager — you'll hear back on this number
          shortly. Enjoy your evening, Rohan!

[Call ends. Zoronal fires webhook → Supabase writes reservation → Telegram pings manager:
"NEW BOOKING — Rohan · party of 4 · tonight 8 PM · quiet corner · 15% discount applied
[CONFIRM] [DECLINE] [I'LL CALL BACK]"]

Journey 2 — Weekend Walk-in Rule

[Customer calls Saturday 11:30 AM wanting to book for the same evening.]

MAYA:     Hi, this call may be recorded. Maya from The Blue Door Cafe —
          reservation, question, or manager?

CUSTOMER: Reservation — Saturday evening, 7 PM, 2 people.

MAYA:     We'd love to have you! Just so you know — on Saturdays and Sundays
          before 1 PM, we don't take advance reservations; it's walk-in only
          for peak hours. The good news is we typically have tables available,
          with around a 15–20 minute wait before noon.

          For your 7 PM visit, that's later in the evening — let me check if
          we can take that booking.

          [check_capacity fires: Saturday 19:00, party 2]

          We do have availability for Saturday at 7 PM. Can I take your name?

[Continues to slot-fill flow.]

Journey 3 — FAQ with Contextual Upsell

[Customer asks about dietary options.]

MAYA:     Hi, this call may be recorded. Maya from The Blue Door —
          reservation, question, or manager?

CUSTOMER: Just a question — do you have vegan options?

MAYA:     Yes! We have vegan health bowls, tofu chimichurri bowls, field trays,
          and several salads. Jain customisation is also possible — just let
          the kitchen know. Full menu is on Zomato if you'd like to browse.

CUSTOMER: That's great.

MAYA:     Would you like me to book a table while we're on the call?
          If it's a weekday dinner, you'd get 15% off by booking here directly.

CUSTOMER: Yes, Sunday lunch, 2 people.

[Continues to slot-fill. Sunday is a weekend — no reservations before 1 PM.
Maya checks the time requested and handles accordingly.]

Journey 4 — Complaint / Escalation

[Customer calls to complain about a previous visit.]

MAYA:     Hi, this call may be recorded. Maya from The Blue Door —
          reservation, question, or manager?

CUSTOMER: I want to speak to someone. I had a really bad experience last week.

MAYA:     I'm genuinely sorry to hear that. Let me make sure the manager
          calls you personally — they'll want to hear this directly.
          Can I confirm you're on this number?

CUSTOMER: Yes.

MAYA:     Got it. I'm marking this as priority. The manager will call you back
          within the hour. Thank you for letting us know — we take this seriously.

[Zoronal webhook → Supabase → Telegram to manager:
"⚠️ PRIORITY CALLBACK — [number] · complaint about previous visit. Call back within 1 hour.
[ACKNOWLEDGED]"]

Journey 5 — Failure / Silent Escalation

[STT fails or caller goes silent for 5+ seconds.]

MAYA:     Hello — are you still there?

[5 more seconds of silence]

MAYA:     I'm having a little trouble hearing you. Let me have someone from our
          team call you back — sorry for the trouble!

[Call logs as 'incomplete'. Telegram to manager: "INCOMPLETE CALL — [number], check and call back."]

7. Functional Requirements

7.1 Voice Agent — Maya

Req IDRequirementPriorityNotes
VA-01Pick up every inbound call within 1.5s of connection on Plivo DIDP0Zoronal handles cold-start; confirmed working on real PSTN
VA-02Open every call with DPDP recording notice + intent routing questionP0Fixed script — not LLM-generated. Verbatim from §9.
VA-03Route to reservation, FAQ, or escalation flow based on first customer turnP0LLM intent classifier in Zoronal prompt
VA-04Default English; switch to Hindi/Hinglish if caller's first turn is in Hindi. Lock for call duration.P0Zoronal secondary language: Hindi
VA-05Slot-fill: name (spell-back confirmed), phone (last 4 confirmed), party size, date, time, special requestsP0Max 2 retries per field before escalation
VA-06Weekend rule: Sat/Sun before 1 PM = walk-in only. Explicitly state this and quote 15–20 min wait. Do not take reservations.P0Hardcoded in prompt, not dynamic
VA-07Call check_capacity tool before confirming any reservation slotP0Returns {available, alternate_slots}
VA-08Mention 15% weekday dinner discount when reservation intent detected (7–11 PM, weekdays)P0Key product differentiator — must be proactive
VA-09Answer FAQs only from knowledge card. Refusal rule: anything not in card → "I don't have that detail, let me have the manager get back to you."P0Kill criterion: <2% false info rate
VA-10Escalate: complaints, modifications, cancellations, groups >15, private events, anything off-scriptP0Collect number, promise callback in 1 hour
VA-11Failure handling: silence >5s or STT failure → graceful escalation, never go silentP0Three failure triggers: silence, STT fail, confidence drop
VA-12Confirm reservation with full read-back before hanging upP0Name, last 4 digits, party size, date, time, special request

7.2 Reservation Management

Req IDRequirementPriority
RM-01Write reservation to Supabase within 3s of call end via Edge Function webhook handlerP0
RM-02Send Telegram notification to manager within 10s of call end with Confirm / Decline / I'll Call Back buttonsP0
RM-03Manager button tap updates reservation status in Supabase immediatelyP0
RM-04Capacity cap: check pending + confirmed bookings per slot vs cap before confirming. Offer alternatives if full.P0
RM-05Partial/incomplete calls (dropped mid-slot-fill) auto-expire after 2 hours. Slot freed. Status = incomplete.P1
RM-06Auto-confirm if manager doesn't respond: 30 min SLA for same-day, 4 hr for future dates (v1)P1
RM-07SMS confirmation to customer on manager confirm; decline + alternative offer on decline (v1, MSG91)P0

7.3 Knowledge Card Management

Req IDRequirementPriority
KC-01Blue Door knowledge card stored as JSON in Supabase. Loaded into Maya's Zoronal prompt at agent config level.P0
KC-02Manager can update knowledge card via WhatsApp (v1): text change → LLM extracts diff → confirm → Supabase update → Zoronal agent prompt update via APIP1
KC-03All knowledge card changes stored with timestamp + author in Supabase (git-style audit)P1

8. Non-Functional Requirements

8.1 Latency

MetricTargetKill Criterion
End-to-end response latency (p50)<2.5s on real PSTN>3.5s p50 → immediate review. Confirmed passing on Zoronal.
End-to-end response latency (p95)<3.5s>4.5s p95 sustained → prompt reduction + voice model review
First-turn pickup<1.5s from call connect to Maya first word>2s → Zoronal cold-start issue
check_capacity tool call overhead<300ms added to turn>800ms → optimise Supabase Edge Function
Telegram notification delivery<10s from call end>60s → check webhook + Telegram API

8.2 Reliability

MetricTargetNotes
Call pickup rate100%Zoronal + Plivo availability. Fallback recording if Zoronal down.
Supabase uptime>99.5%Supabase managed Postgres SLA
Telegram delivery>99%Telegram Bot API. Email fallback for critical escalations.
Reservation data durability100%Supabase Postgres. No reservation can be lost.
Zoronal downtime fallbackPlivo fallback recording"Technical issue, please call back." Customer never gets silence.

8.3 Accuracy

MetricTargetMitigation if Breached
False information rate<2%Kill criterion. Trigger prompt audit + tighten refusal rule.
Reservation data accuracy>95% correct first captureSpell-back + 4-digit confirm mandatory. 2 retries before escalation.
Intent classification accuracy>90%Nightly eval on 20 synthetic calls. Retrain prompt if <90% in week 2.

8.4 Security & Compliance

RequirementImplementation
DPDP Act 2023 — recording consentMaya states recording notice on every call. Stored in calls table with timestamp.
PII at restCustomer phone numbers in Supabase Postgres (AES-256 at rest via Supabase default).
Audio data retentionZoronal retains call recordings 80 days. Transcripts in Supabase retained 1 year.
API key securityAll keys (Zoronal API, Telegram bot token, Supabase service key) in Supabase Edge Function environment variables. Never in code.
Routing integrityEach Plivo DID maps to exactly one Zoronal agent, exactly one restaurant row in Supabase. Hardcoded — not dynamic. Automated routing test before each new restaurant deployment.

9. System Architecture

Senior is a real-time voice pipeline with a thin ops layer. The architecture has three planes:

  • Call Plane: Customer PSTN → Plivo DID → Zoronal (STT + LLM + TTS + agent logic) → check_capacity tool → call end
  • Data Plane: Zoronal webhook → Supabase Edge Function → Postgres (Supabase) ↔ Supabase Studio (owner/manager view)
  • Ops Plane: Telegram Bot (manager notifications + Confirm/Decline) + Zoronal dashboard (call history + recordings) + Supabase Studio (reservation table)
Vendor Portability Rule — Non-Negotiable

Every webhook payload, every transcript reference, every reservation is mirrored to Supabase at the moment Zoronal fires. The Zoronal → Supabase Edge Function boundary is the ONLY point of vendor contact. Replacing Zoronal with Pipecat or any other voice vendor requires rewriting only the Edge Function that receives the webhook. The database layer, the ops layer, the manager flow — all portable. This rule is enforced from Day 1.

9.1 Call Flow

StepComponentWhat HappensLatency Budget
1Plivo / ZoronalCustomer dials Plivo DID. Zoronal routes inbound to Maya agent.0–200ms
2Zoronal TTSMaya speaks fixed DPDP opening line (not LLM-generated — eliminates first-turn spike).200–400ms first audio
3Zoronal STTCustomer speaks. Streaming STT returns partial transcripts. Final on end-of-utterance.300–500ms
4Zoronal LLMIntent classification + response generation. Prompt = Maya system prompt (§9.3).400–700ms
5Zoronal TTSTTS streams from first sentence while LLM generates remainder.200–400ms first byte
6Supabase Edge FnAt date+time+party captured: check_capacity fires. Returns available/full + alternate_slots.<300ms added
7ZoronalLoop continues. Slot-fill state machine tracks fields.—
8Zoronal + Edge FnCall ends. Zoronal POSTs webhook to Supabase Edge Function. Edge Fn writes reservation + fires Telegram.<10s from hangup

9.3 Maya System Prompt — Production Ready (Paste Verbatim into Zoronal)

You are Maya, the AI concierge at The Blue Door Cafe, Khan Market, Delhi.
You handle inbound phone calls — reservations and common FAQs only.

OPEN EVERY CALL WITH THESE EXACT WORDS:
"Hi, this call may be recorded. This is Maya from The Blue Door Cafe —
are you calling to make a reservation, ask a question, or speak to the manager?"

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
KNOWLEDGE CARD — answer ONLY from this list. Nothing outside it.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Address:   66 Khan Market, middle lane, opposite Faqir Chand bookstore, New Delhi.
Hours:     7 AM to 11 PM every day. All-day breakfast available.
Cuisine:   European classics and American favourites — Philly cheesesteak, gourmet burgers,
           healthy salads, bowls, and more. Famous for generous portions.
Price:     ₹2,000 to ₹2,500 for two. Book on this line for weekday dinner (7–11 PM) and
           get 15% off — not available on District, EazyDiner, or Zomato booking.
Dietary:   Vegan: tofu chimichurri bowls, health bowls, salads, field trays.
           Jain: customisable — kitchen can accommodate, just ask.
           Gluten-free: salads, bowls, protein plates. Full menu on Zomato.
           Halal: not certified.
Seating:   No outdoor seating. Smoking area on the second floor.
Alcohol:   Yes — single malts, wine, beer, and more. BYOB not permitted.
Kids:      Welcome. Highchairs and games available. No dedicated kids menu.
Payment:   UPI, cash, and card — all accepted.
Delivery:  Available on Zomato and Swiggy.
Dress:     None. Casual is absolutely fine.
Wait time: 15–20 minutes for walk-ins before 12 PM on Saturdays and Sundays.
Occasions: No decoration setup. Food special requests — we'll align with the kitchen;
           the manager will confirm.
Private:   Escalate to manager.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
REFUSAL RULE — CRITICAL
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
If asked ANYTHING not in the knowledge card above — specific dish prices,
chef names, ownership, GST, alcohol prices, exact dish availability, any topic
not listed — reply EXACTLY:
"I don't have that detail with me. Let me have the manager get back to you
on WhatsApp — what's the best number to reach you?"
NEVER guess. NEVER approximate. NEVER invent. If in doubt, refuse.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RESERVATION RULES
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Weekdays:          Take reservations at any time.
Weekends Sat/Sun before 1 PM:
                   Walk-in ONLY. No advance reservations. Quote 15–20 min wait.
                   Do NOT take a booking for these times.
Weekends after 1 PM: Reservations accepted.
Max party via phone: 15. Groups above 15 → escalate to manager.

RESERVATION FLOW:
1. Collect: name → spell back. Phone → confirm last 4 digits. Party size. Date. Time.
   Special requests.
2. Once date + time + party size collected → call check_capacity tool.
3. If available: confirm the slot, read back all details, mention:
   "Your request is with the manager. You'll hear back shortly."
   For weekday dinner: remind caller about 15% discount if not yet mentioned.
4. If not available: offer alternate_slots from tool response. If customer insists →
   escalate to manager with waitlist note.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ESCALATION — collect number + promise callback for ALL of these:
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Party above 15
- Private event / full buyout enquiry
- Complaint or negative experience (NEVER attempt to handle)
- Modification or cancellation of existing booking
- Request to speak to manager or owner
- Anything outside reservations + knowledge card

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
LANGUAGE + TONE
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Default: English. Switch to Hindi if caller speaks Hindi. Handle Hinglish naturally.
Tone: Warm, friendly, professional. Indian English cadence. No unnecessary filler.

9.6 Supabase Schema (Run as SQL in Supabase Editor)

-- restaurants
create table restaurants (
  id           uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name         text not null,
  short_name   text,
  zoronal_agent_id text,
  plivo_did    text,
  telegram_chat_id text,
  created_at   timestamptz default now()
);

-- knowledge_cards
create table knowledge_cards (
  id            uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  restaurant_id uuid references restaurants(id),
  json_content  jsonb not null,
  version       int default 1,
  updated_at    timestamptz default now(),
  updated_by    text
);

-- capacity_caps
create table capacity_caps (
  id            uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  restaurant_id uuid references restaurants(id),
  day_of_week   text,   -- monday|tuesday|...|saturday|sunday|default
  slot_start    time,
  slot_end      time,
  max_bookings  int
);

-- calls
create table calls (
  id              text primary key,   -- Zoronal call_id
  restaurant_id   uuid references restaurants(id),
  caller_number   text,
  started_at      timestamptz,
  ended_at        timestamptz,
  duration_seconds int,
  intent          text,   -- reservation|faq|escalation|incomplete
  status          text,   -- completed|dropped|failed
  summary         text,
  transcript_url  text,
  audio_url       text,
  created_at      timestamptz default now()
);

-- reservations
create table reservations (
  id                uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  call_id           text references calls(id),
  restaurant_id     uuid references restaurants(id),
  customer_name     text,
  customer_phone    text,
  party_size        int,
  booking_date      date,
  booking_time      time,
  special_requests  text,
  direct_discount   boolean default false,
  status            text default 'pending',
  -- pending|confirmed|declined|auto_confirmed|incomplete
  confirmed_by      text,
  confirmed_at      timestamptz,
  sla_deadline      timestamptz,
  telegram_message_id text,
  created_at        timestamptz default now()
);

Technical Risks

IDRiskSeverityMitigation
T1Zoronal STT degrades on heavy accent or noisy line → wrong slot filledHighMandatory spell-back on name + last 4 digits on phone. If same field asked twice → escalate. Test on real PSTN Day 3.
T2check_capacity tool call adds >800ms → turn latency exceeds 3.5sHighKeep Edge Function lightweight (single Postgres query, no joins). Test call latency Day 3. If slow: move cap check to in-memory lookup.
T3Maya hallucination — states fact not in knowledge cardCriticalRefusal rule is first instruction in prompt. Nightly 20 trap-question eval from Day 5. >2% rate = kill criterion → prompt audit.
T4Zoronal downtime → caller gets no answerMediumPlivo fallback message: "Technical issue, please call back in a few minutes." Owner PagerDuty-equivalent via Telegram alert on webhook silence >60 min.

T6Supabase free tier pauses after 7 days of inactivityLowActive testing and live calls prevent inactivity pause. If paused: manual unpause takes 30 seconds at supabase.com.

UX Risks

IDRiskSeverityMitigation
U1Customer realises AI and feels deceivedHighDPDP recording notice at call open sets expectation. Maya is "AI concierge" — not pretending to be human. If asked directly: "I'm Maya, Blue Door's AI assistant."

U4Caller asks about alcohol prices — Maya refuses, caller frustratedLowExpected behaviour. Refusal is correct. Manager callback resolves. Not a product failure.
